chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, concerning:

A man who doubts, after having performed sajdah, that he did not do ruku'. He said: if he becomes certain, then let him discard the two sajdahs for which there is no rak'ah, then let him continue his salat to completion. And if he did not become certain until after he had finished and departed, then let him stand and perform one rak'ah and two sajdahs, and there is nothing upon him.

The correct way regarding this narration is that we interpret it as referring to one who forgot the ruku' in the last two rak'ahs; then he discards the two sajdahs and completes his salat. But if his forgetfulness was in the first two rak'ahs, then repeating the salat is obligatory upon him, in accordance with what the earlier reports have contained.

key_terms.اسْتَيْقَنَ: became certain rather than merely doubtful
key_terms.السَّجْدَتَيْنِ: the two prostrations belonging to a rak'ah
key_terms.شَكَّ: became doubtful regarding an omission in salat
key_terms.يَرْكَعْ: to perform ruku' in the rak'ah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets the ruku' and only realizes it after sajdah or after finishing the salat?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for one who doubts or realizes that he omitted ruku' after performing sajdah in salat. It distinguishes between cases discovered during the prayer and after finishing, and the concluding legal analysis limits the narration to omission in the final two rak'ahs, while omission in the first two requires repeating the salat.
